title: BMCFuzz: Hybrid Verification of Processors by Synergistic Integration of Bound Model Checking and Fuzzing
problem: RISC-V processor verification requires exhaustive checking of instruction semantics and corner cases, which is computationally expensive using pure formal methods or fuzzing alone.
motivation: Hybrid verification combining bounded model checking (BMC) with fuzzing can achieve deeper coverage more efficiently, reducing design bugs and accelerating processor bring-up.
method: Bounded model checking (formal verification of all possible execution paths up to a fixed depth) identifies the constraints—the rules and limits—that RISC-V instructions must follow. Fuzzing (automated random testing) then uses these constraints to focus on corner cases that the formal method couldn't explore deeply. This creates a feedback loop: formal verification narrows the search space by identifying what matters, and fuzzing scales testing across that narrowed space to catch bugs that either technique alone would miss.
key_novelty: Combining formal verification and fuzzing (automated random testing) with constraints from verification guiding fuzzing's search toward corner cases in RISC-V processors.
contributions: Hybrid BMC-fuzzing framework for processor verification
Constraint-guided fuzzing based on BMC findings
Demonstration of improved coverage and bug detection vs. standalone approaches
limitations: Analysis limited to abstract; specific processor complexity and verification overhead not detailed.
primary_theme: hybrid BMC-fuzzing for RISC-V processor verification
